name: Realistic Rendering
summary: The purpose of this direction is to improve the visual quality of our outputs using high-quality renderers, and eventually differentiable rendering.

tasks.title: Non-Differentiable Fluid Renderer
tasks.note: Implement a non-differentiable renderer which will make our 2D simulation of a fluid look highly realistic. It doesn't need to be fast, it doesn't need to be particularly simple, the purpose of this is just to see how good of something you can make (visually). Under the hood use MPM fluid simulation, and show a few things happening like dropping a fluid ball, or a fluid tower collapse. It should look very realistic, like an actual real-life liquid. Enough to make someone double glance if it was real.

tasks.title: Improve basic fluid sim realism
tasks.note: This simulation rendering looks decent. But the liquid doesn’t really behave like water, it moves a bit too slowly and also the behavior is off, hard to explain exactly. The rendering looks good but there are like holes inside the continuous portions of the liquid, which doesn’t seem right. See if you can push the realism even further. Goal is photorealistic.

tasks.title: Further Realistic Basic Fluid Sims
tasks.note: These results look closer to the photorealistic target, but they are very short and limited. Generate a more diverse and extensive set of examples showcasing the capabilities, such as more starting conditions, different viscosities, even things like mixing liquids of different colors. Also, make the animations much longer, these ones are WAY too short.
